title: Microburst Capacity Simulator and Pricing Playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the Microburst Capacity Simulator (MCS) model, its configuration parameters, and a set of reproducible pricing experiments used to evaluate microburst handling strategies across Redwood’s serving tiers (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to produce deterministic guidance for: 1) capacity commitments, 2) burst-crediting rules, and 3) pricing adjustments that preserve SLOs while minimizing committed cost.

Scope
- Applies to conversational and transactional text-generation endpoints that exhibit sub-minute burst patterns (short spikes lasting 10s–120s).
- Focused on production traffic shapes, pre-production load tests, and billing simulations for pricing policy proposals.
- Not intended for long-term seasonal scaling (multi-hour/day), which falls under predictive-scaling PRDs.

Stakeholders and Owners
- Product (owner): Sofia Martinez (author) — accountable for experiment definitions and commercial recommendations.
- Eng Platform: Jordan Patel — simulator integration and synthetic traffic harness.
- Eng SRE: Amina Chowdhury — SLO alignment and operational guardrails.
- Finance & RevRec: Diego Alvarez — pricing delta analysis and contract language.

Definitions
- Microburst: A short-duration increase in QPS above baseline (10s–120s window).
- Warm Capacity: Reserved capacity that remains allocated to a tenant (committed) to improve tail latency.
- Burst Credits: Consumable credits that allow temporary overage beyond reserved capacity without penalizing latency SLOs.

Problem Statement
Many customers show intermittent high-frequency traffic (e.g., chat spawns from events, batch UX actions, seasonal sign-ups). Current pricing and reserved models are built for steady-state or large-scale predictable bursts, resulting in:
- Over-provisioning (customers buy more reserved capacity than used) or
- Frequent SLO violations during short spikes when requests are routed to slower fallback variants.
We need a quantified, reproducible way to measure the cost vs. SLO tradeoffs for short bursts and design pricing/crediting constructs that align incentives.

Simulator Overview
The Microburst Capacity Simulator (MCS) is a lightweight, deterministic runner that consumes:
- A traffic shape definition (time-series of QPS with event markers)
- A model mix (variants, sequence length distributions, KV cache hit rates)
- Serving node profiles (latency-by-queue depth, GPU memory/slots, preemption characteristics)
- Policies to evaluate (burst-crediting, warm-capacity thresholds, fallback sequencing)

Simulator Outputs (examples)
- Per-second tail (p50/p95/p99) latency time-series per tenant and per route
- Token cost and cost-per-request breakdown by model variant and routing choice
- Warm-capacity utilization curve and credit consumption timeline
- Probability distribution of SLO breaches and implied SLA credit exposure

Core Simulation Parameters (table)
| Parameter | Description | Default (for experiments) | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| baseline_qps | steady-state QPS | 20 | per-route baseline |
| burst_peak_qps | peak during microburst | 200 | 10x baseline typical |
| burst_duration_s | length of burst | 45 | experiment sweep 10, 30, 60, 120 |
| seq_len_p50 | median sequence tokens | 64 | affects per-token compute |
| kv_cache_hit | KV cache hit rate | 0.6 | range tested 0.0–0.95 |
| model_mix | fraction across variants | "v1:0.8,v2-quant:0.2" | v2-quant uses 4-bit quantized path |
| queue_slots_per_node | concurrent requests per GPU | 8 | GPU and runtime specific |
| fallback_policy | ordered list of fallbacks | "same-model,quant,smaller-model" | impacts latency and cost |

Experiment Matrix (examples)
1) Baseline: no burst credits, warm capacity = 0 (pure on-demand routing).
2) Warm small: reserved warm slots = 2 per tenant, no credits.
3) Burst credits: reserved = 0, burst-credit pool = 300 credits/month, credit consumption per request simulated at token granularity.
4) Hybrid: reserved = 1 slot + burst credits = 150/month + automatic canary fallback after 30s.

Pricing and Commercial Experiments
Each experiment produces a per-tenant monthly cost projection (committed + variable) and SLO breach probability. We evaluate three pricing levers:
- Committed slot price (monthly) — lowers variable per-token cost for tenant.
- Burst-credit pack price (prepaid monthly credits) — priced to reflect opportunity cost of holding burst capacity.
- On-demand premium multiplier — increased per-token surcharge when serving from on-demand runtime during sustained bursting (>120s).

Suggested Pricing Structures (examples for discussion)
- Microburst Pack: 500 credits/month for $X — covers ~30 45s bursts at the stated model mix and baseline. Credits priced at ~40–60% of equivalent reserved-slot cost per-minute.
- Persistent Micro Warm: $Y/month for 1 guaranteed warm slot with a discounted token rate; recommended for customers with >10 microbursts/month.
- Auto-topup: excess burst consumption billed at on-demand premium with contextual rollback if exceeded for >5 consecutive bursts.

Acceptance Criteria for Pricing Change
1) Under the hybrid experiment matrix, SLO breach probability must be <= 0.5% p99 latency breach across 95% of customer traffic shapes in our corpus.
2) Median customer cost delta should be neutral or reduce by at least 10% for customers with >6 microbursts/month.
3) Finance-approved revenue model that preserves >=95th percentile margin for hosted tier.

Operational Runbook for Production Rollout
1) Canary (internal): Run MCS-derived policy for 2 internal tenants for 30 days. Monitor: credit burn, p50/p95/p99 latency, model fallback counts.
2) Beta customers: select 5 customers with documented microburst patterns. Offer Microburst Pack vs. Persistent Micro Warm. Collect qualitative feedback.
3) Gradual enablement: enable policy as an opt-in toggle in Console per-tenant.
4) Full rollout: default to conservative hybrid policy with telemetry for 90 days, after which policy becomes a configurable product offering.

Observability and Telemetry Requirements
- New telemetry keys: microburst_event_id, burst_credit_balance, warm_slot_alloc_count, fallback_sequence_used.
- Dashboard: per-tenant burst timeline, credit burn chart, and projected monthly bill delta.
- Alerting: Alert SRE when credit burn rate exceeds 5x projected for >10 minutes.

SLOs and Risk Mitigations
- SLOs: p99 latency target during bursts must be <= 800ms for conversational routes (configurable by tenant).
- If simulated policy shows >1% breach probability in production rollout, automatically throttle new enrollments and revert to baseline routing.
- Guardrail: limit automatic warm-slot assignment to 3 slots per tenant unless signed enterprise contract exists.

Data and Experiment Reproducibility
- All experiments must be captured in the experiment registry (git-backed YAML experiment manifests stored in infra/experiments/mcs/). Each run must include the traffic seed, model catalog snapshot, and serving node profile SHA.
- CLI example to run MCS locally (simplified):

$ rdmcs run --traffic samples/event-demo.json --model-mix v1:0.9,v2-quant:0.1 --profile g4dn-16 --policy hybrid --output results/event-demo-01.zip

Appendix: Example Event Traffic JSON (abbreviated)
{
  "seed": 42,
  "timeline": [
    { "t": 0, "qps": 20 },
    { "t": 300, "qps": 200, "event": "promo_email_open" },
    { "t": 360, "qps": 40 }
  ]
}

Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How are burst credits consumed?
A: Credits are deducted at token granularity based on the on-demand token cost equivalent. Credits are applied after reserved slot capacity is fully utilized.

Q: Will credits be transferable across tenants?
A: No — credits are tenant-scoped to prevent accounting complexity and double-counting.
